question: A discount of 13% on the marked price of an article is allowed and then the article is sold for ₹348. The marked price of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given, Selling Price (SP) = ₹348 and Discount = 13%.

Marked Price (MP) = SP × [100 ÷ (100 − D%)]

MP = 348 × [100 ÷ (100 − 13)]

MP = 348 × (100 ÷ 87)

MP = 4 × 100 = ₹400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
 
 Marked Price (MP) = 100%
 
 Selling Price = 87%
 13% Off

 

 SP = ₹348

 

 MP = ?

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of the article = ₹348

Discount offered = 13%

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP − Discount

Discount = MP × (Discount % ÷ 100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) of the article be x.

⇒ SP = x − (13% of x)

⇒ SP = x × (1 − 13 ÷ 100)

⇒ 348 = x × (87 ÷ 100)

⇒ x = (348 × 100) ÷ 87

⇒ x = 4 × 100

⇒ x = 400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Selling Price

Marked Price (MP) is the list price or tag price printed on the article. Selling Price (SP) is the amount received after deducting the discount. SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the single equivalent discount percentage is given by: [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.

Profit & Loss Baseline

While discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), Profit and Loss are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specified otherwise.
